headline: Chips Surge While Homebuilders Slump in a Lopsided Tuesday Tape
body_html:
Tuesday's session was a tale of one hot corner and a cooler everything else. The semiconductor group climbed 3.29%, easily the best of the eight sectors we track, yet the wider market finished slightly negative: 250 stocks rose and 272 fell among the 526 in our universe.

Leadership was concentrated in the hardware chain. Fabrinet, an optical-components maker, jumped 15.45% to top the board. FormFactor gained 10.87% and Advanced Energy rose 9.63%. Forgent Power Solutions added 10.50% and Everus Construction 9.46%, which suggests the appetite reached the power and construction work surrounding that hardware. Industrials rose 0.44% and healthcare 0.29%.

The money came from elsewhere. Homebuilders sank 3.68%, consumer shares lost 1.17%, and materials and software each slipped about two-thirds of a point. Software also produced the ugliest single-stock moves: Dynatrace fell 14.69%, Gartner 13.19% and Shopify 8.74%. With Election Day and Mideast headlines in the background, investors paid up for a narrow set of winners and sold much of the rest. Wednesday opens with that split unresolved.

briefs.headline: Optical Supplier Tops the Leaderboard
briefs.body: Fabrinet surged 15.45%, the largest gain in our universe on Tuesday. The move stood out even in a strong day for chip-linked names, where the semiconductor group as a whole gained 3.29%. Buyers clearly favored companies tied to the hardware supply chain.

briefs.headline: Chip Equipment and Power Names Join the Rally
briefs.body: FormFactor climbed 10.87% and Advanced Energy rose 9.63%, showing the semiconductor advance reached beyond chipmakers themselves. Forgent Power Solutions gained 10.50% in the industrial power niche. The common thread was suppliers rather than end-product sellers.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Take the Heaviest Hit
briefs.body: Homebuilders fell 3.68%, the weakest sector we track and more than three times the drop in consumer shares, down 1.17%. The slide stood out against modest gains in industrials and healthcare, and marked the sharpest divergence on the board.

briefs.headline: Software and Research Names Hit Hard
briefs.body: Dynatrace dropped 14.69% and Gartner fell 13.19%, while Shopify lost 8.74% and HealthStream 8.42%. The software sector overall slipped 0.67%, so the pain was concentrated in a handful of stocks rather than spread evenly across the group.

briefs.headline: Oil Wobbles on Reports of US Strikes on Iranian Island
briefs.body: Oil edged higher after officials described US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island as defensive. Iran said contacts on ending the conflict continue, though the latest talks produced no breakthrough. Energy shares finished a touch lower, down 0.16%.

briefs.headline: Overseas Markets Lean on Softer Oil
briefs.body: Indian shares extended gains on easier oil prices and strong earnings, and Canada's TSX rebounded as an oil pullback lifted industrial and mining stocks. Meanwhile the dollar drifted on Mideast and midterm-election worries, and the Australian dollar dipped after an expected rate hike.
